speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal X-ray shows dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, which strongly suggests a distal obstruction like Hirschsprung disease or meconium ileus. To differentiate between these, I need to know if there was any polyhydramnios during pregnancy or if the infant has any physical stigmata of cystic fibrosis, such as a positive newborn screen or family history. REQUEST TEST: Contrast Enema

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal contrast enema makes Hirschsprung disease less likely, so I suspect meconium ileus, which is often the first sign of cystic fibrosis. Do you have a family history of cystic fibrosis, or was a newborn screening performed for this condition? REQUEST TEST: Sweat Chloride Test

speaker: Doctor
text: With a normal sweat chloride test, cystic fibrosis is unlikely, so I am now considering meconium plug syndrome or another functional obstruction. REQUEST IMAGES
